subject: Cross-team status for QBR: wins, risks, and action requests
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-team status for QBR: wins, risks, and action requests

Team —

Attaching a concise snapshot for this week's exec staff review and QBR prep. Please skim the wins/risks and call out any items that need escalation before Friday (10/30). Attachment: QBR_materials_v3.pdf (deck + appendix).

Wins:
- Dedicated rollout: Redwood Dedicated pilot for Acme completed p95 latency target for steady-state workloads (see attachment, slide 6).
- Optimize suggestions: Redwood Optimize recommended a quantization profile that is showing a 22% token-cost reduction in staging (INF-987).
- Console: token-level breakdown is live for all internal routes (small UI follow-up scheduled next sprint).

Risks / open blockers:
- Latency regression: a subset of long-sequence requests are seeing tail latency spikes during bursts; root cause trending toward KV-cache eviction under mixed workloads. Impact: potential SLO misses for enterprise tenants.
- QBR appendix: we need customer-facing SLA language approved for Acme by legal procurement (acme.procurement@acme-enterprises.com) to finalize slide 12.
- Marketplace listing: cloud partner needs final pricing matrix for October marketplace sync (contact: cloud-partner@cloudx.io).

Asks (action items / owners / due dates):
- Markus: provide a short write-up on KV-cache mitigation & temporary throttling rules by Thu 10/29 EOD. (Attachment: service-latency-chart.png)
- Laura: confirm negotiation stance on SLA credits for Acme and share any approved redline guidance by Thu 10/29 noon.
- Vivek: prioritize an ops runbook for burst-eviction scenarios and share triage playbook by Fri 10/30.
- Grace: consolidate QBR appendix into final deck and upload to the Drive link below by Fri 10/30 3pm PT.

Notes: I pulled the metrics across Dedicated and Hosted clusters to avoid cross-mix anomalies; see INF-987 for query logs and sampling.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/link-to-qbr-deck
Atlassian: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-987

Thanks —
Maya Srinivasan
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-team status for QBR: wins, risks, and action requests

Thanks Maya — quick read, looks solid. A couple clarifying points: 

- For the latency regression, when you say "subset of long-sequence requests" can you quantify (e.g., >1k tokens or specific customer cohorts)? We need a clear statement for the QBR slide.
- On SLA language for Acme: procurement is already pushing for a credits-first approach. I'm going to draft a fallback position (no credits, service credit capped) unless legal flags. Laura will own language and loop in legal.

I'll aim to have a proposed negotiation note by Thu 10/29 11:30am.

Onwards —
Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Cross-team status for QBR: wins, risks, and action requests

Looping in CloudX for transparency on marketplace pricing impact.

Maya / team — quick technical note on the KV-cache tail spikes:
- Reproduction shows edge-case where mixed batch sizes cause aggressive cache churn; the p95 remains fine but p99 jumps when bursts coincide with large context jobs.
- Mitigation options (short list): 1) temporary background prefetch + pinning for enterprise routes, 2) soft backpressure on very large contexts, 3) staged TTL bump for recently used KV entries.

I'll draft a 1-pager and attach to INF-987 by Thu EOD. If CloudX needs a consolidated note for their marketplace listing, happy to provide a short blurb.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick responses — plan below and confirmations: 

1) Markus: thanks — that mitigation list is perfect. Please add the 1-pager to INF-987 and I'll flag the technical appendix slide.
2) Laura: please proceed with your negotiation note. If legal signs off on a capped-credit approach, we'll reflect that in slide 12.
3) Vivek: can you take point on the runbook and leave a short README in the runbook folder (link in INF-987) so CS can triage quickly? Target Fri 10/30 EOD.
4) Grace: please merge the finalized appendix into QBR_materials_v3.pdf and re-upload to the Drive link; I'll confirm final deck distribution once legal & tech notes land.

Acme / CloudX: copying you to keep procurement & marketplace owners in the loop. If either of you need a short readout before Friday, reply and we'll slot 15 minutes on calendar.

Deliverables and deadlines summarized:
- INF-987: Markus 10/29 EOD (KV-cache 1-pager + service-latency-chart.png)
- Negotiation note: Laura 10/29 11:30am (SLA credit stance)
- Ops runbook README + triage playbook: Vivek 10/30 EOD
- Final QBR appendix / deck upload: Grace 10/30 3pm PT

I'll consolidate and send a final deck to exec distro on Sat 10/31 morning PT.

Thanks all —
Maya
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
